title: Integral open direct image preserves constructibility
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and the separated finite-type $k$-scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\pi_E$, and residue field $\mathbf F_E=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion of schemes in this setting [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. On their small pro-étale sites use the completed coefficient sheaves $\mathcal O_{E,T}=p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_T$ and the constant finite sheaves $\mathbf F_{E,T}$, for $T=U,X$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. Use the derived module direct image [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], bounded constructible categories [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible, sk-def-sfb-constructible], and their finite Tor amplitude subcategories [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. If $K\in\Dbc(U,\mathcal O_E)$, then $Rj_*K$ is derived complete [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], the canonical finite-reduction comparison is an isomorphism
$$
(Rj_*K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}\mathbf F_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_*(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,U}}\mathbf F_{E,U}),
$$
and $Rj_*K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)=\Dctf(X,\mathcal O_E)$.

proof.text: Apply the internal integral residue criterion to K on U and on X. The finite-type hypotheses give Noetherian schemes by Mathlib. Obtain completeness of K, bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude of its actual first reduction, and the integral finite-Tor equality on X.

The internal direct-image-limits theorem makes the specified scalar mate chi invertible, preserves completeness, and makes the displayed geometric adjunct invertible. For any map c satisfying the displayed counit equation, cancel chi; injectivity of the inverse adjunction Hom equivalence forces c to equal that adjunct. Thus the invertible comparison exists uniquely.

The uniformizer generates the maximal ideal of the integer DVR. Since the spectral absolute value extends the p-adic norm, l has norm less than one and is zero in the residue quotient. The maximal ideal is open (the norm is continuous), so the residue quotient topology is discrete; it is finite by the finite quotient theorem. Apply finiteOpenDirectImage_constantModel_torAmplitude to the first reduction, enlarging its Tor interval to ordered bounds.

Use the unique comparison isomorphism to transfer residue bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude to the actual reduction of Rj_*K. Isomorphism invariance is the well-definedness theorem. Together with completeness, the residue criterion gives integral bounded constructibility. Its equality clause supplies the last conclusion.
